newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Energy, drugs shares pull Budapest BUX lower.
newsitem.headline: Energy, drugs shares pull Budapest BUX lower.

text.p: Share prices closed lower for the second successive day on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) due to profit-taking, traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,646.60 points, down 60.85.
BUX index futures settlement prices slipped for four maturities, rose for one and remained steady also for one, BSE figures showed.
Traders said oil and gas company MOL led the profit-taking on the spot share market.
"The price falls were evidently due to profit-taking, primarily in MOL," said Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB Rt.
"Others fell because of psychological reasons as they followed MOL," he said. He added MOL recently rose to what he called irrealistic heights.
On Monday MOL ended at 1,665 forints, down 65.
Pharmaceuticals maker Richter was among the shares which followed MOL.
"There was a similar phenomena with Richter," Santha. "It had risen to 8,500 forints from 8,000 forints very quickly recently and this rise encourages quite many people to lock in profit," he said.
Other losers included Inter-Europa Bank which ended at 38,100 forints, down 400.
